metaData.originalTitle: 空间智能初探：重建与生成的双路径实践
metaData.title: Exploring Spatial Intelligence: Dual Pathways of Reconstruction and Generation
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the exploration journey of Professor Peng Junran's team at the University of Science and Technology Beijing over the past three years in the field of world models, gradually building a technology stack towards 4D world models through 3D scene reconstruction, intelligent content generation using graphics engines, and 4D volumetric video generation.
metaData.summary: This article is compiled from a speech by Dr. Peng Junran, Associate Professor at the University of Science and Technology Beijing, at QCon 2026 Beijing. Starting from the endgame judgment of artificial intelligence, the article argues that language intelligence will replace everything possible in the virtual space within five to ten years and will inevitably radiate into the physical space. The world model is key to closing the loop from cognition to physical execution. Since 2023, the team has been exploring three technical routes in parallel: large-scale scene reconstruction based on 3D Gaussian Splatting, optimized by introducing geometric priors and material properties to enable physical simulation capabilities; intelligent content generation based on graphics engines, using Agent-driven approaches to automatically generate complete scenes from language descriptions, applied in autonomous driving simulation and embodied intelligence services; and video generation-assisted reconstruction, addressing reconstruction degradation in sparse views through iterative refinement. Ultimately, the team proposed a 4D world model system, where a feed-forward 4D generation model and a spatial refinement model iterate with each other to generate free-viewpoint dynamic volumetric videos from 2D videos, fundamentally eliminating spatiotemporal inconsistencies. The article points out that an end-to-end 4D generation model is the ideal ultimate form.

mainPoints.point: The world model is key to closing the loop from cognition to physical execution, requiring three capabilities: deducing the future, internalizing physical laws, and offering rich forms of expression.
mainPoints.explanation: Large language models can talk but cannot act. The world model provides a closed loop from action to observation, serving as a bridge between cognition and the physical world. An ideal world model should be able to deduce causality, understand physical laws, and interface with various forms of observation and interaction.

mainPoints.point: The team explored three technical routes in parallel—3D reconstruction, graphics engines, and video generation—gradually building the technology stack towards a 4D world model.
mainPoints.explanation: 3D reconstruction provides explicit geometric representation but lacks interactivity; graphics engine generation creates scenes compatible with industrial pipelines but relies on manual work; video generation lacks geometric constraints. The team advanced all three routes in parallel, ultimately merging them into a 4D world model system.

mainPoints.point: The 4D world model achieves generation from 2D videos to free-viewpoint dynamic volumetric videos through iteration between a feed-forward 4D generation model and a spatial refinement model.
mainPoints.explanation: The system takes 2D videos or single images as input and outputs a 4D Gaussian representation containing spatiotemporal dimensions. Through repeated iterations of feed-forward generation and spatial view refinement, it converges to a high-quality, spatiotemporally consistent representation, fundamentally eliminating spatiotemporal inconsistencies.

mainPoints.point: The explicit 4D representation holds immense value for embodied intelligence and autonomous driving simulation, directly providing 3D/4D trajectories without the need for inverse solving.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional 2D generation models require additional inverse solving to obtain spatial trajectories, whereas in 4D representation, trajectories are primitive. In autonomous driving, it can output multiple geometrically consistent camera videos at once and supports scene editing operations.

keyQuotes: Language intelligence, or the generative capability of AI, will inevitably replace everything that can be replaced in the virtual space within five to ten years.
An end-to-end 4D generation model is our ideal ultimate form.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Because the underlying representation is explicit 4D, spatiotemporal inconsistencies are fundamentally eliminated.

relatedArticles.title: Li Xiang × Luo Yonghao! Li Xiang's Ideal: Using AI Technology to Give Ordinary People a Life of Luxury
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Li Auto founder Li Xiang delves into the company's strategic logic for transforming from an automaker into an AI and embodied intelligence company, technical breakthroughs in self-developed chips and full-by-wire chassis, and his predictions for the endgame of autonomous driving and humanoid robots.

relatedArticles.title: Jensen Huang's GTC 2026 Keynote Transcript: All SaaS Companies Will Disappear; Lowest Token Cost Globally; "OpenClaw" Made History; Feynman Architecture is on the Way
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Jensen Huang unveiled the Feynman architecture and Vera Rubin platform at his GTC 2026 keynote, emphasizing that AI has entered the era of inference and intelligent agents, and predicting the transformation of SaaS to AaaS.

relatedArticles.title: JD.com Ad Large Model in Practice: How the GRAM Architecture Delivers Generative Recommendations in Under 50ms
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: JD.com's advertising team unveils the GRAM architecture, which achieves generative recommendations within 50ms by directly aligning intent with product semantics, employing fast and slow dual-pathways, leveraging knowledge engineering, and optimizing engineering, while effectively mitigating hallucinations.

relatedArticles.title: When the Primary User of a Database is No Longer Human: Our Architectural Practices and Reflections in AI Agent Scenarios
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores the architectural challenges arising when AI Agents become the primary users of databases, shares TiDB's practical experience in cost control, long-context storage, and architectural simplification, and introduces mem9, a memory layer infrastructure designed for Agents.

relatedArticles.title: #509. In-depth Interview with Former ByteDance Researcher: The Real Gap in China's AI, Benchmark Culture, and the New Frontier of AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A former ByteDance researcher, now an assistant professor at Peking University, offers a deep analysis of China's AI landscape: the gap between China and the US is widening, not narrowing; benchmark culture masks real-world model usability; data distillation is both a shortcut and a trap; and AI agents and embodied intelligence represent potential breakthroughs.

relatedArticles.title: 134. A Deep Dive into Data with Xie Chen: The History, Landscape, Pyramid, and Recipe of AI and Robotics Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A deep dive into the paradigm shift of AI and robotics data, exploring how simulation data acts as an 'educational system' to solve the data desert problem in embodied AI, and defining the future symbiotic landscape of brains, bodies, scenarios, and data.

relatedArticles.title: QuantumBit Exclusive Interview with Lou Tiancheng: AI is a Runaway Horse, and Harness is the Most Critical Skill of This Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pony.ai CTO Lou Tiancheng elaborates on the core philosophy of the PonyWorld World Model 2.0: when AI driving capabilities surpass humans, the value of human data drops to zero, AI must become the 'head coach' leading R&D, and the ability to harness this 'runaway horse' of AI will be the most critical skill of this era.

relatedArticles.title: CIOs Are Abandoning AI Code Generation Rate: A Practical Review of What Truly Counts as R&D Efficiency
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a year of practical experience, the Alibaba Cloud CIO team proposes that the core of R&D efficiency in the AI era lies in 'scaling' rather than 'code generation rate.' By implementing left-shifted quality testing, knowledge engineering, API specifications, and Half-Stack role restructuring, they achieved a 3x increase in effective code output per frontend developer, 2x for backend developers, and a 30%-55% reduction in defect rates.

relatedArticles.title: The Stronger AI Gets, the More Lost Enterprises Become: 10 Real Questions from Top CIOs
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through in-depth dialogues between Alibaba Cloud's CIO and CXOs from over 40 leading enterprises, this article reveals ten core dilemmas in enterprise AI implementation, covering key dimensions such as technical boundaries, knowledge engineering, organizational transformation, and R&D efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: 139. [Agent Overview] A Conversation with Su Yu on the History of Agent Technology, the OpenClaw Moment, the Blurring of Boundaries, and Societal Impact
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Professor Su Yu from The Ohio State University provides an in-depth review of the complete technological evolution of AI Agents, from logical agents to language agents. He interprets the similarities between the OpenClaw Moment and the ChatGPT Moment, and predicts that Agent technology will evolve towards a Universal Digital Agent, driving the democratization of technology.
